name: EPCIS-MutBench
description: Electronic Product Code Information Services (EPCIS) standardizes inter-organizational supply-chain visibility events, yet structurally conformant histories can contain contradictory lifecycle claims that undermine information integrity. We present EPCIS-MutBench, a controlled benchmark and layered validator for evaluating security-relevant semantic and lifecycle integrity in EPCIS 2.0.1 histories. Mutations are treated as integrity violations independently of accidental or adversarial origin; the benchmark evaluates detection and localization rather than attacker attribution. The evaluation uses 2000 deterministic clean histories and 20,000 primary mutants, including 16,000 single-fault and 4000 compound cases, with validator-independent typed ground truth. Across all primary mutants, JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Schema plus compatibility-projected GS1 Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL) detected 18.27%, whereas the full event-local and role-aware lifecycle validator detected 95.29%. Among 13,429 single-fault mutants that passed both structural baselines, the full validator achieved 92.98% recall, with end-to-end intended-rule, event, and field/edge localization of 92.90%, 92.19%, and 92.14%, respectively. No false positives occurred on the 2000 generated-clean controls; however, in a separate sensitivity analysis that provisionally treated all 37 parseable external-source fixtures as clean, 19 were marked invalid.
